findings.issue: This is a user-visible change to a shipped verb, and neither the changelog nor the compatibility record mentions it. `audit-task.py scope <id> --gate Y` on a task whose tests.gate holds entries Y leaves out used to exit 0 and replace the list. It now exits 2 and writes nothing (`_scope_gate_refusal`, audit-task.py:10207-10244). New behaviour: `--gate-add`, the success-line clause 'tests.gate now holds [...]', and the `gateNowHolds` key in --json. COMPATIBILITY.md's contract covers the manifest and the config only, and `--gate` is still read, so no promise is broken. But the document records every earlier exit-code move on an audit-task verb 'because an exit code moved from 0 to 2 on a shipped command, and a pipeline that read ... is a pipeline that now stops' (COMPATIBILITY.md:546-556). The repo's precedent P153-R3 filed the missing CHANGELOG line for a `--gate*` behaviour change as a finding. No caller inside the repo is broken: commands, agents, skills, the drive (drive-phase.py only builds `scope --files` argvs, :3203 and :6817), tools, examples and .github build no `scope --gate` argv, and the suite's own replace-meaning callers (sn4, gc3, jf, fg1, fg3, dg4b, gx1) now pass --replace.
findings.resolution: Scope CHANGELOG.md and COMPATIBILITY.md into the task. Add an [Unreleased] '### Changed' entry: `scope --gate` refuses a list that leaves out a held entry unless --replace (exit 2, nothing written). Add an '### Added' entry for `--gate-add` and `gateNowHolds`. Add a COMPATIBILITY.md not-promised bullet, in the shape of the existing 'which FLAGS a verb accepts ... and it changed' entry, naming the exit-code move and the repair (`--replace`, or `--gate-add`).

findings.issue: The validator's wide-gate warning fires when a task's tests.gate is its phase's testGate verbatim. It tells the operator to 'Narrow it to the paths this task names ... go through `/audit:task scope <id> --gate "<command>"`'. A narrowed list leaves out held entries by definition, so after this diff that exact call is refused without --replace. This file is outside the diff, but the diff changed the verb on the other side of that instruction. The executor disclosed this, and the plan gate refused the edit. The refusal names --replace, so the cost is one round trip.
findings.resolution: Scope _manifest_phases.py, and tests/test__manifest_phases.py if a case pins the text, into this task or a follow-up. Say that narrowing takes `--gate "<command>" --replace`, while declaring the wide gate as the answer (the same list, which drops nothing) still takes a bare `--gate`.

findings.issue: `--gate-add Y` on a task that declares no gate of its own writes `[Y]` with gateBasis `declared`. Such a task has tests.gate absent, `[]` or all-blank, gateBasis not `cleared`, and `_mio.gate_entries` (_manifest_io.py:663-692) measures it by the phase's testGate. So the gate that grades the task silently shrinks from the phase's entries to `[Y]`. Yet the help text, task.md and verbs-in-full describe --gate-add as appending 'keeping every entry the task holds'. `_held_gate` and `_gate_added` read only the stored list, never the resolved one. This is the class this task closes: a call spelled as 'keep' loses entries the gate ran. The success line prints `[Y]` but not what it replaced.
findings.resolution: In `_locked_scope`, when `_held_gate(node)` is empty and `_mio.gate_entries(phase, node)` returns source 'phase' with entries, do one of two things. Either refuse `--gate-add`, naming the phase gate it would replace and the spelling that keeps it (`--gate <each phase entry> --gate Y`), or seed the append with those resolved entries. Add a gk case on such a task that tells the two outcomes apart.
